doc.title: Denny Zeitlin interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002

title: Intuitive rather than cerebral approach to learning jazz
summary: He started formal harmony in about sixth grade but learned jazz by osmosis, soaking up Chicago clubs and quizzing pianists.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Not formally at the beginning. I didn’t start really formally studying harmony probably until I was in maybe sixth grade. So it was more intuitive, what I was doing with the music. And even after I started to formally study harmony, my approach to the music has always been more of an intuitive one. Sometimes people imagine because I’m a © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-

psychiatrist and a doctor that gee that’s a cognitively demanding pursuit, and I must be a real cerebral kind of guy. And it’s really not very descriptive of me. My approach to the music, my approach to learning jazz was not a didactic one at all. It was like experiential, it was osmotic. I would go down to these clubs in Chicago and stay out until five in the morning and just soak it up. Grab a piano player after the gig and say, “come on, show me, what did you play, how did you voice that chord?” I mean that was how I learned this music. Not from some school. Not from some book. That didn’t speak to me.
